beliefs: The cubic is nearly odd: f(-x)≈-f(x) for |x|>=2.6, e.g. f(-128)≈8175362 vs -f(128)≈8181913 [E1]
There is a special interval roughly |x|<2 where f deviates strongly from the cubic and is not odd: f(1.2)≈-2.5, f(1.5)≈-5.5, f(1.9)≈-18.8 while f(-1.2)≈7.2, f(-1.5)≈11.6, f(-1.9)≈27.4 [E2, E3]
The transition to the cubic regime happens near |x|≈2: f(2)≈-25 fits cubic, f(1.9)≈-18.8 close to cubic, but f(1.5)≈-5.5 is far from cubic [E2, E3]

The negative-side values in E3 differ from E2 at same x (e.g. f(-1.2)=7.22 vs 9.32, f(-1.5)=11.55 vs 14.09), suggesting noise or a steeper-than-cubic local shape; exact form inside |x|<2 not pinned down? [E2, E3]
notes: Kept cubic for |x|>=2.6 and refit the near-zero polynomial to include E3 points, which shifted the negative-side curve toward the new observations while preserving the E1/E2 bumpy shape.
